reason: zod memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections (npm audit range < 4.6.6); no patched zod 3.x exists as of 2026-10-24 - 3.25.76 is both the vulnerable ceiling of the 3.x line and its newest stable release on npm (the 3.26.0-canary prereleases above it are unpatched too). The two remaining zod 3.25.76 copies are node_modules/expo/node_modules/zod (required by @expo/cli, the Expo CLI, which imports zod only in its dev-server DevTools and MCP schemas) and node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-compiler/node_modules/zod (required by the dev-only lint plugin eslint-plugin-react-compiler and its zod-validation-error). Neither is app code: every zod import under src/ resolves to the top-level node_modules/zod, which is 4.6.7 and held there by package.json ^4.6.7. This allowance is keyed by advisory id, so it would also cover a top-level copy below 4.6.6; that package.json range is the only guard on it.
upstream: npm's suggested remediations are semver-major DOWNGRADES (expo@54.0.38 for the Expo CLI copy, eslint-plugin-react-compiler@0.0.0 for the plugin copy), rejected per the capped-floor doctrine; a floor cannot close it either, since no patched 3.x exists to cap it at. Re-read 2026-11-07: @expo/cli 57.0.33 (published 2026-11-05) moved zod to devDependencies (npm view @expo/cli@57.0.33 dependencies.zod is empty, devDependencies.zod ^3.25.76) and expo 57.0.32 (the same day) requires @expo/cli ^57.0.33, so the node_modules/expo/node_modules/zod copy leaves with an expo bump inside the repo's ~57.0.27 range once min-release-age=3 allows it (from 2026-11-08); package-lock.json still holds expo 57.0.27, so the copy is installed today. The other copy stays: eslint-plugin-react-compiler has had no release since 2025-08-15 (the installed 19.1.0-rc.2 is its latest tag, and its dependency on zod 3 is unchanged), and no stable zod 3.x past 3.25.76 exists (npm view zod versions). Re-check at expiry: npm view zod versions for a stable 3.x release past 3.25.76, an expo release that pulls @expo/cli 57.0.33 or later (the expo copy), or a new eslint-plugin-react-compiler release that drops zod 3. If none exists, re-date with a fresh reading.

reason: decode-uri-component denial of service through quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs (GitHub rates it high, published 2026-10-29, vulnerable range <=0.5.0, first patched 0.5.1). The installed copy is 0.2.2 and it reaches this tree only through expo-router -> query-string@7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component. That is app runtime code: expo-router's own build code uses query-string to parse a URL's query into route params (getStateFromPath, behind its linking config for deep links). No fix is adoptable today: the patched line, 0.5.0 and 0.5.1 (published 2026-06-29 and 2026-10-23), is ESM only (type module, a default export, no CommonJS entry), while query-string 7.1.3 is CommonJS, declares ^0.2.2 and calls the result of require('decode-uri-component') as a function. Measured under Node 24.16.0 with the installed query-string pinned to 0.5.1, require() returns an object with __esModule and default and queryString.parse throws TypeError: decodeComponent is not a function (Metro and jest were not tried). npm's own remediation is a semver-major, an Expo SDK move. Re-read 2026-11-07: still ESM only at 0.5.1 (npm view decode-uri-component@0.5.1 type exports: type module, default export only); query-string 7.1.3 is still the newest 7.x and is CommonJS on ^0.2.2, 8.2.0 and 9.4.1 are type module on ^0.4.1 (also in the vulnerable range), and 10.0.0 no longer depends on decode-uri-component but is not what expo-router asks for (expo-router 57.0.30, the newest 57.x, still declares query-string ^7.1.3). This allowance expires sooner than the others, 2026-11-21, because the code ships in the app.
upstream: npm's suggested remediation is expo-router@58.0.30 (as of 2026-11-07; its dependencies no longer list query-string), a semver-major that is an Expo SDK move (scripts/version-holds.json holds expo-router to 57.x), rejected per the capped-floor doctrine; an override to the patched 0.5.x is no alternative, since that line is ESM only and query-string requires it from CommonJS. Re-check at expiry: npm view expo-router versions for a 57.x release, or npm view query-string versions for a release, that takes decode-uri-component >= 0.5.1, or an override proven to work under Metro and jest. If none exists, re-date with a fresh reading.
